question: Can a class-balanced LightGBM relevance filter over web pages keep more relevant pages in an agent's top-5 context while reading fewer characters than a standard TF-IDF retrieval baseline?
method: Posts from 20 Newsgroups (headers/footers/quotes removed) are pages truncated to 1,500 characters; categories are split into training and unseen test categories; category names are queries. Both models rank the test pages per query; metric is precision@5 with success@5 and tokens read as secondary metrics.
baseline: TF-IDF cosine similarity retrieval, top-5 pages (RAG-style retriever).
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM classifier trained on query-page pairs from training categories, with TF-IDF cosine, cosine relative to the query's best score, within-query z-score and rank of the cosine, query-term coverage, LSA (100-dim TruncatedSVD on TF-IDF, fitted unsupervised per pool) cosine and its within-query z-score, and log page length; ranks test pages by predicted probability, top 5.
notes: Stand-in corpus, not the paper's web-agent setup (no LLM agent, no real web pages). Only seven test queries, so results are high-variance; the reported std only reflects LightGBM seed variation, not the choice of category split. Test categories are 7 of 20 (35% of categories, a deliberate category-level split), which is above the 20-30% guideline. Vectorizers and LSA are fitted unsupervised on each pool's pages; the TF-IDF baseline is unchanged. Hyper-parameters were chosen by query-level CV on training categories only; the test pool was never used for selection. fetch_20newsgroups has no timeout option, so a 60 s socket timeout and retry/backoff wrap the download.
